title: Assessment triage record (draft 0.1.0)
description: The record of triaging one subject before it is assessed: the answers to the triage questions, the tier each risk driver gives, the resulting assessment type and risk tier (the highest any driver gives), any override, and the assessment plan that follows. The tier is derived again from the design specification once it is complete, and the derived tier wins. Draft: see standards/assessment/standard-assessment-triage.md.

id.description: TR-NNN. Proposed by this draft and not yet in the envelope.

design.description: The design specification, once there is one.

supersedes.description: The earlier triage of the same subject, when this is a re-triage after a change.

reach.description: Required when uses_model is true: what the most capable model-backed element can touch.

agency.description: Required when uses_model is true: how far it acts without a person, after AWS's Agentic AI Security Scoping Matrix.

untrusted_content.description: Untrusted content in a model's context, and what else the same session can do.

platform.description: The assessed platform the subject runs on, if any, and whether the subject sits inside its envelope.

target_state.description: The target-state position of each building block the subject uses, attested by the architect responsible for the target architecture it belongs to. Never inferred by the author or by an assessor. CORE-TGT-01 reads it, and triage derives novelty from it.

element.description: The element's id in the subject's design specification.

ref.description: The catalogue identifier, when the building block is catalogued.

position.description: target: part of the target architecture. in-flight: on its way to it. baseline: in the landscape today but not target, with a successor to come. retiring: on a dated path out. retired: not to be used. not-target: neither in the landscape today nor part of the target architecture, so a design that uses it brings in technology the target does not plan for.

successor.description: What replaces it in the target state, when it is not target and the architect has named it.

permitted_use.description: The use the position holds for, when the architect limits it: for example, a platform that is target only for running one kind of workload. Use beyond it is a departure.

role.description: For example enterprise architect, or the domain architect for the platform.

type.description: stopped: a prohibited practice; the subject is not assessed for approval.

drivers.description: The tier each driver gives. The result's tier is the highest of them, or the override.

override.description: A tier raised above the high-water mark. Tiers are never lowered.

inherits.description: Criteria met by inheritance from the assessed platform, inside its envelope.

lenses.description: The lenses of the assessment about to run. The production lens joins only the production entry assessment.

tier.description: AT1 Light, AT2 Standard, AT3 Enhanced, AT4 Critical. Not the guardrail tiers T0 to T3.
